protocol.dataset: Same pinned THCHS-30 source as mandarin_protocol.json; no new download required
protocol.selection: Up to 10 unique source-word tokens per phone/speaker, deterministic hash order; consonants 40–400 ms, vowels 160–400 ms. Exact central 160 ms of original continuous audio, with adjacent context for short phones. Exclude windows and playable word crops with >1% samples at amplitude >0.99 or window AC RMS <0.002. Preserve old 30/10/10 speaker assignment. Previously held-out speakers were used to report the first nine-sound map; this extension is not a claim of never-before-inspected corpus speakers.
protocol.encoder: qwen-asr-large, chosen in the previous Mandarin study; no new encoder sweep
protocol.layout: Fixed display grid: vowels, fricatives, sonorants, stops, affricates in separate rows; class labels placed left to right in listed family order. Arbitrary supervised display coordinates, not articulatory axes. All views share one fitted coordinate system.
protocol.candidates: Training-fitted standardization and PCA128/256, followed by class-balanced Ridge alpha100 or smooth MLP regression (128 hidden tanh units, L2 alpha1, learning_rate_init0.001, maximum250 iterations, internal early stopping; training speakers only). Select by validation nearest-center balanced accuracy in the final two display coordinates; save selection before final test. Refit only the selected method on development speakers.
protocol.evaluation: Report all 28-class and per-class test recalls, family means, 1000 speaker bootstrap interval; 20 tokens per phone on final test for +/-20 and +/-40 ms timing shifts. Adjacent vowels can supply information; this is consonant-containing-window discrimination, not context-free articulation assessment. Corpus phone timestamps are approximate.
protocol.ui: Preserve original map as an option. Expanded map has all 21 initials + final ng + six vowels; family filters only change region visibility, not coordinates or inference. 160 ms rolling window and 40 ms hop, one inference in flight with stale windows discarded; short events leave a longer visible trail. No claim of automatic phoneme boundary detection or articulatory feedback.
